mechanism_narrative: The four-week monotonic rise in RETAIL_REC from -40.7 to -26.9 reflects removal of mobility constraints and creates habitual footfall momentum; the next four-week mean will be higher than the last four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly mean rose from -40.7 at t-3w to -26.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing above -25 percent marks resumption of discretionary trips; retail footfall follows transit with a two-week lag, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -25 percent
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -35.0 at t-3w to -20.1 at t-0w and crossed -25 at t-0w
failure_condition: After TRANSIT rises above -25 percent, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility improves and RESIDENTIAL mobility falls, households shift from home to out-of-home leisure; this substitution raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -40 percent and RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 percent
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -52.6 to -34.9 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 19.1 to 13.7
failure_condition: When PARKS is above -40 and RESIDENTIAL below 15, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM normalizing above zero while RETAIL_REC remains deeply negative signals pent-up discretionary demand; as essential shopping normalizes, spending rotates into retail and recreation.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 0.0 to 19.0 and RETAIL_REC rose from -40.7 to -26.9
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM > 10 and RETAIL_REC > -30, the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Policy reopening is observed as simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES; office and commuting return expands weekday retail catchments, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -35.0 to -20.1 and WORKPLACES from -29.0 to -22.3
failure_condition: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by >2 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The three-week improvement in PARKS from -52.6 to -34.9 reflects a seasonal spring transition toward outdoor leisure; this seasonal lift raises retail-and-recreation footfall over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -52.6 at t-3w to -34.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the next week is not higher than its mean over the last 28 days despite three consecutive weekly PARKS improvements.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains above 12 and GROCERY_PHARM above 15, home-centric stockpiling persists and diverts trips away from discretionary retail, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 13.7 and GROCERY_PHARM is 19.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL > 12 and GROCERY_PHARM > 15, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC crossing above -30 percent is an operational reopening threshold; once crossed, venue reopenings accelerate and the next four-week mean exceeds the previous four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC weekly mean rises above -30 percent
failure_condition: After RETAIL_REC crosses above -30, its mean over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.
